fact_en:
Why are many sharks in danger?

Because people catch too many of them worldwide, especially just for their fins.
fact_bis:
Ngano nga namiligro ang daghang iho?

Tungod kay sobra silang gipangdakop sa mga tawo sa tibuok kalibotan, ilabi na para lang sa ilang mga kapikas.

findings.note: Sharks-in-danger card: EN 'especially just for their fins' becomes 'ilabi na para lang sa ilang mga kapikas' — kapikas means mate/partner (corpus uses it that way in 37 cards, e.g. ffct-00276, ffct-02433). Fins are palikpik/kapay everywhere else in the corpus (66 fin cards). A child reads that sharks are over-caught 'just for their mates'; the finning fact is destroyed and nothing in the card restores it.

fact_en: Measles spreads very easily, but the MMR vaccine protects against it along with mumps and rubella.
fact_bis: Sayon kaayong makatakod ang tigdas, apan ang bakuna nga MMR nanalipod batok niini, ug usab sa baki ug German measles.

findings.note: MMR card: 'nanalipod batok niini, ug usab sa baki ug German measles'. baki = frog/toad in this corpus (185 cards, incl. ffct-10459 in this same batch). Mumps is rendered beke everywhere else (ffct-00400 'mumps (beke)', ffct-02413 titled 'Beke'). The card never says beke/mumps, so the child learns MMR protects against measles, frogs and German measles — one of the three diseases is lost.

fact_en:
Can you catch schistosomiasis just by touching a sick person?

No! You can't catch schistosomiasis just by living together or holding hands. The parasite must first pass through a snail and water before it can reach another person.
fact_bis:
Matakod ba ang schistosomiasis kon hikapon nimo ang masakiton?

Dili! Dili ka matakdan sa schistosomiasis pinaagi lang sa pagpuyo og hiniusa o paggunit og kamot. Kinahanglan mo-agi una ang parasito sa kuhol ug tubig una kini makaabot sa lain nga tawo.

findings.note: title_bis 'Schisto Dali Hawak' reads as schisto being easily caught by touch/contact - the exact myth the card exists to debunk (title_en: 'Schisto Not by Touch'). Looks like 'Dili' corrupted to 'Dali'; also 'hawak' is waist in Cebuano, not touch (hikap/gunit, as the body uses). Body does say 'Dili!', so a full reader recovers it, but the heading alone states the opposite health claim.

fact_en:
Do hollow bones make birds float on water?

Not really! Light bones help a little, but the bigger reason birds float is their feathers and the air trapped in them.
fact_bis:
Molutaw ba ang langgam tungod kay hawan ang buto niini?

Dili gyud! Makatabang ang gaan nga buto, apan ang mas dako nga hinungdan sa paglutaw mao ang mga balhibo ug hangin nga nasulod niini.

findings.note: Body uses Tagalog 'buto' for bone twice ('hawan ang buto niini', 'gaan nga buto'). Cebuano for bone is 'bukog' (which title_bis correctly uses); Cebuano 'buto' means explode / seed / vulgar genitals, so the question 'Molutaw ba ang langgam tungod kay hawan ang buto niini?' names a different thing in a kids' card. Title restores the fact, so lower severity, but the swap is wrong for Cebuano in general.

fact_en:
Why does a hermit crab carry an anemone?

Some hermit crabs carry a sea anemone on their shell — its stinging tentacles scare enemies away and help keep the crab safe.
fact_bis:
Nganong adunay dalang anemone ang uban umang?

Adunay mga umang nga nagdala og anemone sa ilang kabhang — ang makapaso nga galamay niini nakahadlok sa mga kaaway.

findings.note: title_bis 'Anemone sa Ermitanyo' translates 'hermit crab' as 'ermitanyo' - a hermit/recluse person, not an animal. Body correctly says 'umang', so the fact is recoverable, but the title names a different thing (same class as the cat card titled 'iro').

fact_en:
What is really stored inside a bulb?

The food stored inside a bulb is mostly sugar and starch that the leaves made using sunlight.
fact_bis:
Unsa ba gyud ang gitipig sulod sa bombilya?

Ang pagkaon nga gitipig sa bombilya kasagaran asukal ug almirol nga gihimo sa mga dahon gikan sa kahayag sa adlaw.

findings.note: Plant bulb rendered as 'bombilya' (electric light bulb) in BOTH title_bis ('Bumbilya Asukar Dahon') and body ('Unsa ba gyud ang gitipig sulod sa bombilya? Ang pagkaon nga gitipig sa bombilya...'). Nothing in the Cebuano names a plant part, so a child reads that sugar and starch are stored inside a light bulb. The English is about an onion-type storage bulb. Unrecoverable from the card.

fact_en:
Why is it called brain coral?

Brain coral has winding ridges and grooves on its surface that together look just like a human brain — that's how it got its name.
fact_bis:
Ngano gitawag kining brain coral?

Ang brain coral adunay liko-liko nga mga tubo ug kinhason sa ibabaw niini nga nagkasamang morag utok sa tawo — mao nga mao ang iyang ngalan.

findings.note: EN 'winding ridges and grooves on its surface' becomes 'liko-liko nga mga tubo ug kinhason sa ibabaw niini'. 'Kinhason' is shellfish/seashells, a completely different thing, and 'tubo' (pipe) is not a ridge. The card asserts brain coral has shellfish on its surface and never corrects it; only the 'looks like a brain' part survives.

fact_en: Your digestive system is a team: mouth, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine all work together to break down food and absorb nutrients.
fact_bis: Ang digestive system usa ka team: baba, esophagus, tiyan, gagmay nga tinai, ug dako nga tinai — magkauban nga nagpurito sa pagkaon ug nagsuyop og sustansya.

findings.note: EN: "...all work together to break down food and absorb nutrients"; BIS: "...magkauban nga nagpurito sa pagkaon ug nagsuyop og sustansya". `purito` is not a word in this corpus at all (0 of 49,156 cards; the corpus renders "break down food" as pagtunaw / magbungkag / pagdugmok / naglata across 52 cards), and the nearest reading for a child is `prito` = fried, so the Cebuano body says the mouth, esophagus, stomach and intestines FRY the food. The tl row has it right ("nagtutunaw ng pagkain"), so this is bis-specific. Partial mitigation: title_bis "Sistema sa Paghilis" still says digestion, so a child may recover the topic but not the mechanism.

fact_en:
Why are pitcher plants so brightly colored?

Pitchers are often brightly colored like flowers so they can attract insects more easily.
fact_bis:
Ngano nga mabulokon ang mga tabo?

Ang mga tabo kasagaran mabulokon nga morag bulak aron mas madani ang mga insekto.

findings.note: EN: "Why are pitcher plants so brightly colored? Pitchers are often brightly colored like flowers so they can attract insects more easily." BIS: "Ngano nga mabulokon ang mga tabo? Ang mga tabo kasagaran mabulokon nga morag bulak aron mas madani ang mga insekto." The Cebuano never says tanom / pitcher plant anywhere in the body — the subject is only ever "tabo", which to a Cebuano child is the water dipper (or a market day, tabo-an). The English question line anchors it with "pitcher plants"; the Cebuano question line drops that anchor. The only other anchor is title_bis "Nepenthes", a Latin name a grade-5 child will not know. Corpus check: 34 pitcher-plant cards use "tabo" only for the cup and always with "pitcher plant" / "tanom" adjacent in the same sentence (e.g. "sa sulod sa tabo sa pitcher plant") — this card is the one where the anchor is missing, so the child is told dippers are brightly coloured to attract insects. Slug not a word-pair, because "tabo" for the cup itself is fine when anchored.

fact_en:
Does a platypus's venom come from its bill?

No! A platypus doesn't bite to inject venom — the venom is actually in a sharp spur on the back of its leg.
fact_bis:
Gikan ba sa sungo ang hilo sa platypus?

Dili! Ang platypus dili mopaak aron mohilo; ang hilo niini naa sa hait nga tibo sa likod sa iyang tiil.

findings.note: title_bis "Tuko Dili Tuka sa Platypus" for title_en "Venom Spur Not Bill". In Cebuano tuko = GECKO — the corpus itself uses tuko as gecko in 53 cards ("Tiil sa Tuko", "Tuko vs Butiki"), and renders spur as "tibo", including in this card's own answer ("ang hilo niini naa sa hait nga tibo sa likod sa iyang tiil") and in the sibling platypus cards ("Tibo Platypus Kirot", "Venom Spur Platypus"). The title therefore reads "Gecko Not Beak of the Platypus" — a different animal named on the card. Same defect recurs in ffct-* "Echidna nga Tuko Walay Hilo" (Echidna's Harmless Spur), so spur->tuko is wrong in general, not a one-off.

fact_en:
What is the animal kingdom called?

It's called Animalia! This big group includes birds, fish, and even us humans.
fact_bis:
Unsay tawag sa gingharian sa mga mananap?

Gitawag kining Animalia! Nalakip dinhi ang mga langgam, isda, ug bisan ang mga tawo.

findings.note: title_bis 'Animalia Gingharian Tawo' for title_en 'Animalia Kingdom Animals' - the title says the Animalia kingdom is HUMANS ('tawo') instead of animals ('mananap'). Body is correct ('gingharian sa mga mananap'), but the title names the wrong group.

fact_en: Eating fatty food sends a signal to your gallbladder, telling it to release bile into your intestine to help digest it.
fact_bis: Kon mokaon ka og tambok, adunay senyas nga madawat sa gallbladder aron ipagawas ang apdo ngadto sa tinai.

findings.note: title_bis 'Matabang Pagkaon sa Bile' for title_en 'Fatty Food Frees Bile'. In Cebuano 'matabang' means BLAND/insipid (cf. 'tubig-tabang' = freshwater in ffct-11128), the opposite of the trigger described; fatty is 'tambok', which the body does use. The title therefore states that bland food releases bile.
